entities.name: PMID:25085325
observations: 2014 study comparing otosclerotic stapedial osteoblasts (n=11), normal stapedial osteoblasts (n=4), and human normal-bone osteoblasts (n=13) in vitro.
Alendronate was tested at 10^-10 to 10^-8 M; adhesion, proliferation, mineralization, and osteoblast/bone-remodeling gene expression were measured.
Untreated otosclerotic cells had greater adhesion and calcification but lower proliferation than controls; osteopontin expression was 9.4-fold lower than normal stapedial osteoblasts at day 14.
Alendronate dose-dependently normalized adhesion, proliferation, and mineralization to control levels, increased osteopontin, and decreased the RANKL/OPG ratio.

entities.name: Alendronate
observations: In the otosclerotic stapedial osteoblast study, alendronate normalized the principal measured cellular phenotypes in vitro and corrected reported osteopontin and RANKL/OPG abnormalities.
Normalization of every osteoblast-marker gene was not established in the accessible abstract.

entities.name: Alendronate phenotype normalization
observations: In vitro, alendronate brought otosclerotic stapedial osteoblast adhesion, proliferation, and mineralization to levels equal to normal stapedial and normal-bone osteoblasts.
The evidence supports normalization of the major measured functional differences, but not necessarily every gene-expression endpoint.
